```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

# Set timezone
Sys.setenv(TZ = "Asia/Tokyo")
```


# 1. Introduction
This analysis explores the relationships between the CAD/JPY exchange rate and macroeconomic indicators in Canada and Japan from 2004 to 2023.


# 2. Libraries
```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)
```



# 3. Load Data
```{r load_data}
# Load processed data
df <- read.csv("processed_data.csv")
```



# 4. Scatter Plot Analysis
## 4.1 GDP vs CAD/JPY
```{r gdp_scatter_plots}
# Canada
gdp_plot_ca <- ggplot(df, aes(x = gdp_CA / 1e12, y = cad_jpy)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "green") +
  labs(
    title = "Canada",
    x = "GDP (Trillion USD)",
    y = "CAD/JPY Exchange Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Japan
gdp_plot_jp <- ggplot(df, aes(x = gdp_JP / 1e12, y = cad_jpy)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "green") +
  labs(
    title = "Japan",
    x = "GDP (Trillion USD)",
    y = "CAD/JPY Exchange Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Display both plots
grid.arrange(
  gdp_plot_ca,
  gdp_plot_jp,
  ncol = 2,
  top = "GDP vs CAD/JPY"
)
```
Japan's GDP shows a negative relationship with the CAD/JPY exchange rate, while Canada's GDP shows a weaker relationship.


## 4.2 Inflation Rate vs CAD/JPY
```{r inflation_scatter_plots}
# Canada
infl_plot_ca <- ggplot(df, aes(x = infl_CA, y = cad_jpy)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "green") +
  labs(
    title = "Canada",
    x = "Inflation Rate (%)",
    y = "CAD/JPY Exchange Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Japan
infl_plot_jp <- ggplot(df, aes(x = infl_JP, y = cad_jpy)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "green") +
  labs(
    title = "Japan",
    x = "Inflation Rate (%)",
    y = "CAD/JPY Exchange Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Display both plots
grid.arrange(
  infl_plot_ca,
  infl_plot_jp,
  ncol = 2,
  top = "Inflation Rate vs CAD/JPY"
)
```
Both Canada and Japan show positive relationships between inflation rates and the CAD/JPY exchange rate.


## 4.3 Unemployment Rate vs CAD/JPY
```{r unemployment_scatter_plots}
# Canada
unemp_plot_ca <- ggplot(df, aes(x = unemp_CA, y = cad_jpy)) +
  geom_point(color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "green") +
  labs(
    title = "Canada",
    x = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    y = "CAD/JPY Exchange Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Japan
unemp_plot_jp <- ggplot(df, aes(x = unemp_JP, y = cad_jpy)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "green") +
  labs(
    title = "Japan",
    x = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    y = "CAD/JPY Exchange Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Display both plots
grid.arrange(
  unemp_plot_ca,
  unemp_plot_jp,
  ncol = 2,
  top = "Unemployment Rate vs CAD/JPY"
)
```
Canada's unemployment rate shows a negative relationship with the CAD/JPY exchange rate, while Japan's unemployment rate shows a weaker relationship.


# 5. Correlation Analysis
```{r correlation_analysis}
# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficients
cor_results <- data.frame(
  Indicator = c("GDP", "Inflation Rate", "Unemployment Rate"),
  Canada = c(
    cor(df$gdp_CA, df$cad_jpy),
    cor(df$infl_CA, df$cad_jpy),
    cor(df$unemp_CA, df$cad_jpy)
  ),
  Japan = c(
    cor(df$gdp_JP, df$cad_jpy),
    cor(df$infl_JP, df$cad_jpy),
    cor(df$unemp_JP, df$cad_jpy)
  )
)


# Display correlation results
knitr::kable(cor_results, digits = 3)
```



# 6. Summary
Japan's GDP and Canada's unemployment rate show negative correlations with CAD/JPY, while inflation rates in both countries show positive correlations. Canada's GDP and Japan's unemployment rate show weak correlations.
